subject: Integration in the context of environmental variation

messages.author: 06349ef2b6713bb8
messages.subject: Integration in the context of environmental variation
parts:
Hi all


I’m examining the influence of environmental variables on hind leg weapon variation in male monkey beetles. I have specimens and environmental data from nine sites, and I’m interested in looking at whether differences in weapon form between sites align with differences in habitat variables (e.g. size of the flowers that the beetles fight on) between those sites.


I’ve captured landmarks for the femurs, tibias, tarsae and tarsal claws in separate files and have so far analysed patterns of shape and size variation for each of these leg segments separately, using mixed models in R with the lme() function. But in the real world, these different leg components are of course interacting and being used in combination with one another in males’ battles. I want to be able to assess whether they exhibit modularity and if so, covariation with one another. I have used geomorph’s integration.test and modularity.test functions to do so, and there does seem to be a case for each leg component to function as a module that exhibits integration with the other leg component modules (to a greater or lesser extent) (see sample plot below). What would really tie in nicely with the rest of the story, however, would be if it were possible to assess whether leg components are more or less integrated depending on differences in environmental variables between the sites in which specimens were collected from. I.e. is there a correlation between environment and morphometric integration? The thinking behind this is that the beetles live, feed and fight on asteraceae and aizoaceae flowers – both disc-shaped – that provide a fighting arena. Arena size as well as other-site specific variables may influence optimal fighting style, which in turn may select for different types of hind leg component ‘elaboration’ in different populations.


I do have phylogenetic data that is in preparation and am keen to explore modularity and integration in a phylogenetic context once that data is ready.


Thanks in advance!


Kind regards

Ariella

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Integration in the context of environmental variation
parts:
Ariella, I´m not sure there was a question to be answered in your message, but if you want to compare the degree of integration across datasets you may want to have a look at the function compare.pls and at this paper: Adams, D.C. and M.L. Collyer. 2016. On the comparison of the strength of morphological integration across morphometric datasets. Evolution. 70:2623-2631.

Hope this helps

Antigoni
